## R13, the open sub-step · σ is generated by inner fluctuation, because the lepton is the fourth colour

**The question.** R13 (third pass) showed that σ is *forced* on the Tree's Pati–Salam 16 and that,
with it, the window gives m_H = 125.20 GeV. It left open whether the Tree's structure *generates*
σ, or whether σ is added by hand, as Chamseddine–Connes did in 2012.

**How it was tested.** In a spectral triple (A, H, D, J), the bosonic fields are the inner
fluctuations D → D + A + JAJ⁻¹, with A = Σ π(a)[D, π(b)]. A Majorana entry T of D produces a field
that rescales it, which is σ, only if T fails to commute with the algebra. The Tree's estate has no
cascade Dirac operator (capstone L18, L19), so the test builds the two finite spectral triples that
carry its walked branch, on the Tree's fermions:
- H = 16 ⊕ 16̄ per generation, in the bimodule form of Chamseddine, Connes and van Suijlekom (CCvS
  2013);
- generic Yukawas (colour-blind for quarks, distinct for the lepton);
- the Majorana entry ν_R → ν̄_R.

| Algebra | [T, π(a)] | Majorana-block fluctuations | σ among them? | First-order condition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard Model, ℂ ⊕ ℍ ⊕ M₃(ℂ) (the lepton is not a colour) | 0 for every a | none (dimension 0) | **no** | holds exactly |
| Pati–Salam, ℍ_R ⊕ ℍ_L ⊕ M₄(ℂ) (the Tree's walked branch, L11, with L13's lepton as fourth colour) | nonzero | 15 complex entries (30 real) | **yes** | fails, exactly at T |

The Pati–Salam fluctuations fill the entries (antiparticle in 2_R, lepton colour) ← (particle s = 0,
any colour) and their J-images. These are two copies of a field in (2_R, 1, 4), sharing the ν_R ν_R
entry, which is σ. This is CCvS's Δ_{ȧI} ∈ (2_R,1_L,4), whose composite ΔΔ lies in the (3_R,1_L,10)
that R13 Part A found by covariance.

**What makes the Majorana entry fluctuate.** The algebra directions that fail to commute with T are:
- the **leptoquark directions** of M₄ (lepton ↔ quark colour);
- the **B−L direction**;
- **right-handed isospin** (ℍ_R).

Colour SU(3) and left-handed isospin commute with it.

**Verdict.** σ is not put in by hand on the Tree's walked branch: it is an inner fluctuation of the
Majorana entry. It exists *because* the Tree treats the lepton as the fourth colour (**L13**, a
GENUINE link) and because the branch is Pati–Salam with right-handed isospin (**L11**). In the
Standard-Model algebra, which has no such unification, the same entry commutes with everything and
σ cannot arise, which is why the 2012 paper had to add it.

Together with R13 Parts A and B, the chain now reads:

> L11 + L13 → the Majorana entry fluctuates → σ (generated) → the window gives m_H = 125.20 GeV at a
> seesaw-consistent scale.

**What stays open.** The Tree's estate has a KO-6 spectral triple for Mₙ(ℂ) on a four-block space
(L18), but nothing yet connects the cascade's Hilbert space to the Pati–Salam triple used here. That
connection is L18's own open part, and it is now the single remaining step between the cascade and
σ. L15 stays PARTIAL.

## R12 · Weinberg 3/8 from Chain Theory's offices — refuted

**Pre-registered (v1 §6.9).** If Chain Theory's W and Z offices are the traces Tr(T₃L²) and Tr(Q²) on
its particle webs, their ratio is 3/8 at the unification reading and 3/5 at the hypercharge reading.
*Kill-condition:* a different ratio from the same offices.

**Chain Theory's text.**
- Theorem 164.5: the office of the W word over the office of its two-line read is "the exact rational
  one half", which Chain Theory reads as the squared cosine of the weak angle.
- Its other candidate readings are 2/3, 1/3 and ½ (per family, 164.4) and 17/36 and 14/36 (165).
- Its own Standard-Model table grades the weak mixing angle "silent".

**Verdict: refuted at the kill-condition.** None of these ratios is 3/8 or 3/5, whether read directly
or as a complement: ½ as cos² gives sin² = ½. So Chain Theory's offices are not the Tree's trace
forms, and the Weinberg value 3/8 (the Tree's L17, a trace identity on the 16) has no counterpart
among them. No grade moves.

## R1′ · The closed triangle, formalised — done

`closed_triangle_attachments_le_three`: the three qutrit sites are `Fin 3`, every pair is linked, and
the core ends at site s are indexed by the other two sites (`card_other_sites`: exactly 2). With the
valence law (Q4's Theorem A), the triangle admits at most three attachments. The "two core ends per
site" that Theorem C′ took as input is now derived from "closed triangle". The count of three in
Chain Theory's 197.3 therefore rests, on the Tree's side, on one network fact (the triangle is
closed) and one theorem (the valence law).
